business_problem: On-premises reporting across SQL Server and mainframe systems made performance data hard to use and left Penske without a secure, practical way to turn many operational indicators into actionable manager guidance.
solution_summary: Penske Logistics moved reporting and generative AI workloads onto Snowflake on Azure so operational, safety, and workforce data could be analyzed together and summarized at scale. The company centralizes indicators from logistics systems, telematics, and other business sources in Snowflake, replacing limited SQL Server and mainframe reporting with a scalable cloud platform. Business analysts and leaders now use self-service reporting over companywide data spanning five years, while data scientists build repeatable analysis processes on the same governed foundation. Penske then uses Cortex AI to run LLMs directly inside Snowflake, turning nearly 30 dashboard columns into concise talking points and recommendations for each associate without bringing in an external AI vendor. Because the models stay in Snowflake’s governed perimeter, the team launched its first summarization model in less than 15 days and gave managers faster insight to improve safety, performance, and retention.
